title: Cell: The Unit of Life
syllabus: Cell theory and cell as the basic unit of life; Structure of prokaryotic and eukaryotic cell; Plant cell and animal cell; Cell envelope, cell membrane, cell wall; Cell organelles - structure and function; Endomembrane system - Endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi bodies, Lysosomes, Vacuoles; Mitochondria, Ribosomes, Plastids, Microbodies; Cytoskeleton, Cilia, Flagella, Centrosome and Centrioles; Nucleus - nuclear membrane, chromatin, nucleolus.

questions.question: Who among the following scientists modified the cell theory to its final shape by explaining that cells divide and new cells are formed from pre-existing cells (Omnis cellula-e cellula)?
questions.solution: Rudolf Virchow (1855) first explained that cells divide and new cells are formed from pre-existing cells (Omnis cellula-e cellula). He modified the hypothesis of Schleiden and Schwann to give the cell theory its final modern shape.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the chemical constituents and historical findings of cell biology:

List-I (Scientist / Model)List-II (Contribution / Year)
(A) Antonie van Leeuwenhoek(I) Fluid Mosaic Model of plasma membrane (1972)
(B) Robert Brown(II) First saw and described a live cell
(C) Singer and Nicolson(III) Discovered and named the cell nucleus (1831)
(D) George Palade(IV) Discovered ribosomes under electron microscope (1953)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Antonie van Leeuwenhoek first saw and described a live cell; Robert Brown discovered the nucleus in 1831; Singer and Nicolson proposed the Fluid Mosaic Model in 1972; George Palade discovered ribosomes under electron microscopy in 1953.

questions.question: Which of the following layers of the prokaryotic cell envelope determines the shape of the bacterium and provides strong structural support to prevent it from bursting or collapsing?
questions.solution: In prokaryotes, the cell wall determines the shape of the cell and provides strong structural support to prevent the bacterium from bursting (in hypotonic medium) or collapsing. Glycocalyx provides protection/adhesion, and plasma membrane acts as a semipermeable barrier.

questions.question: Mesosomes in prokaryotic cells are specialized membranous structures formed by the invagination of the plasma membrane. Which of the following is NOT a function of mesosomes?
options: Protein synthesis by transcription and translation
Cell wall formation and DNA replication
Increasing the surface area of the plasma membrane and enzymatic content
questions.solution: Mesosomes help in cell wall formation, DNA replication, distribution of daughter chromosomes, respiration, secretion, and increasing enzymatic surface area. Protein synthesis is carried out by 70S ribosomes in the cytoplasm, not by mesosomes.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the prokaryotic surface appendages and structures:

List-I (Structure)List-II (Feature / Function)
(A) Bacterial flagellum(I) Elongated tubular structures made of special pilin protein (mating/conjugation)
(B) Pili(II) Composed of filament, hook, and basal body; enables active motility
(C) Fimbriae(III) Non-membrane bound reserve material storage in cytoplasm
(D) Inclusion bodies(IV) Small bristle-like fibres sprouting out to help attach bacteria to rocks/hosts

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Flagellum: Locomotory organelle composed of filament, hook, and basal body; Pili: Tubular structures for bacterial conjugation; Fimbriae: Bristle-like surface attachments for sticking to substrates/hosts; Inclusion bodies: Non-membranous storage bodies (e.g., phosphate, cyanophycean, and glycogen granules).

questions.question: According to the Fluid Mosaic Model of Singer and Nicolson (1972), the quasi-fluid nature of lipids enables:
options: Lateral movement of proteins within the overall lipid bilayer (membrane fluidity)
Complete flip-flop movement of all peripheral proteins across the membrane
Rigid, impermeable barrier formation for all polar and non-polar solutes
Covalent binding of all carbohydrates directly to the interior hydrophobic core
questions.solution: The quasi-fluid nature of the phospholipid bilayer enables lateral movement of integral and peripheral proteins within the overall bilayer. This ability to move within the membrane is measured as its fluidity, which is essential for cell growth, formation of intercellular junctions, secretion, endocytosis, and cell division.

questions.question: In human erythrocyte (RBC) membrane, biochemical investigation shows that the membrane consists of approximately:
questions.solution: Chemical studies of human red blood cell (erythrocyte) membranes reveal that they contain approximately 52 per cent protein and 40 per cent lipids, with the remainder composed of carbohydrates.

questions.question: Middle lamella, the cementing layer holding neighbouring plant cells together, is primarily composed of:
questions.solution: The middle lamella is a layer mainly consisting of calcium pectate (and magnesium pectate) that glues the adjacent plant cell walls together.

questions.question: Which of the following sets of cell organelles are included in the Endomembrane System because their functions are strictly coordinated?
options: Endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi apparatus, Lysosomes, and Vacuoles
Endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi apparatus, Mitochondria, and Chloroplasts
Golgi apparatus, Lysosomes, Vacuoles, and Peroxisomes
questions.solution: The endomembrane system includes Endoplasmic Reticulum (ER), Golgi complex, Lysosomes, and Vacuoles because their functions are coordinated. Mitochondria, Chloroplasts, and Peroxisomes are not coordinated with these and are not considered part of the endomembrane system.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the functions of the Endoplasmic Reticulum (ER):

List-I (Type of ER)List-II (Characteristic Function)
(A) Rough Endoplasmic Reticulum (RER)(I) Synthesis of lipids, phospholipids, and steroid hormones
(B) Smooth Endoplasmic Reticulum (SER)(II) Active protein synthesis and secretion; studded with 80S ribosomes

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Rough Endoplasmic Reticulum (RER) bears 80S ribosomes on its outer surface and is actively involved in protein synthesis and secretion. Smooth Endoplasmic Reticulum (SER) is devoid of ribosomes and is the major site for synthesis of lipids and steroid hormones.

questions.question: Proteins synthesized by ribosomes on the endoplasmic reticulum are transported to the Golgi apparatus, where they enter at the ________ and, after post-translational modification, leave from the ________:
questions.solution: Proteins fuse as transport vesicles with the cis (convex/forming) face of the Golgi apparatus, move through the cisternae where glycosylation takes place, and are finally packaged and released as vesicles from the trans (concave/maturing) face.

questions.question: Lysosomes are membrane-bound vesicular structures formed by the packaging process in the Golgi apparatus. Their hydrolytic enzymes (hydrolases) are optimally active at:
questions.solution: The isolated lysosomal vesicles contain rich hydrolytic enzymes (lipases, proteases, carbohydrases, nucleases) capable of digesting all macromolecules. These enzymes are optimally active at an acidic pH maintained by proton pumps.

questions.question: In plant cells, the central vacuole is bounded by a single semipermeable membrane called:
questions.solution: In plant cells, the large central vacuole can occupy up to 90 per cent of the volume and is bounded by a single transport-active membrane called the tonoplast, which facilitates the transport of ions against concentration gradients into the vacuole.

questions.question: In Amoeba, which organelle is responsible for osmoregulation and excretion of excess water?
questions.solution: In Amoeba, the contractile vacuole is important for osmoregulation and excretion. Food vacuoles are formed by engulfing food particles.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the structural components of Mitochondria:

List-I (Component)List-II (Feature / Function)
(A) Outer membrane(I) Contains circular dsDNA, 70S ribosomes, RNA, and Krebs cycle enzymes
(B) Inner membrane(II) Continuous, smooth, forms the limiting boundary of the organelle
(C) Cristae(III) Infoldings that increase the surface area for ETS complexes and ATP synthase
(D) Matrix(IV) Encloses the inner aqueous compartment

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Outer membrane: Smooth outer boundary; Inner membrane: Selectively permeable internal boundary enclosing matrix; Cristae: Infoldings of the inner membrane that increase surface area for ATP synthesis; Matrix: Dense fluid compartment containing circular DNA, 70S ribosomes, and TCA cycle enzymes.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the types of Plastids and their stored nutritional materials:

List-I (Plastid Type)List-II (Stored Nutrient Material)
(A) Amyloplasts(I) Oils and fats
(B) Elaioplasts(II) Proteins
(C) Aleuroplasts(III) Carbohydrates (starch, e.g., potato)
(D) Chromoplasts(IV) Fat-soluble carotenoid pigments (carotene, xanthophylls)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Amyloplasts: Store starch (carbohydrate); Elaioplasts: Store oils and fats; Aleuroplasts: Store proteins; Chromoplasts: Contain fat-soluble carotenoids giving yellow, orange, or red color to plant parts.

questions.question: In chloroplasts, flat membranous sacs arranged in stacks like piles of coins are called ________, and the fluid ground matrix surrounding them is called ________:
questions.solution: In chloroplasts, thylakoids are flattened membranous sacs arranged in stacks called grana (singular: granum). The surrounding gel-like fluid matrix containing Calvin cycle enzymes, 70S ribosomes, and circular DNA is called the stroma.

questions.question: Ribosomes are non-membrane bound granules composed of ribonucleic acid (rRNA) and proteins. The sedimentation coefficients of eukaryotic and prokaryotic ribosomes are respectively:
options: 80S (composed of 60S and 40S subunits) and 70S (composed of 50S and 30S subunits)
70S (composed of 50S and 30S subunits) and 80S (composed of 60S and 40S subunits)
80S (composed of 50S and 30S subunits) and 70S (composed of 40S and 30S subunits)
70S (composed of 60S and 40S subunits) and 80S (composed of 50S and 30S subunits)
questions.solution: Eukaryotic cytoplasmic ribosomes are 80S (consisting of 60S large and 40S small subunits). Prokaryotic ribosomes (as well as organellar ribosomes of mitochondria and plastids) are 70S (composed of 50S large and 30S small subunits). 'S' stands for Svedberg unit (sedimentation coefficient).

questions.question: The cytoskeleton in a eukaryotic cell is an elaborate network of filamentous proteinaceous structures. Which of the following is NOT a primary function of the cytoskeleton?
options: Synthesis of ATP and oxidative phosphorylation
questions.solution: The cytoskeleton (microfilaments, microtubules, and intermediate filaments) provides mechanical support, motility, and maintenance of cell shape. ATP synthesis and oxidative phosphorylation are performed by mitochondria.

questions.question: An axoneme of a eukaryotic cilium or flagellum is characterized by which of the following arrangements of microtubules?
options: $9 + 2$ doublet arrangement (9 peripheral doublets + 2 central single microtubules)
questions.solution: The core of a eukaryotic cilium or flagellum, called the axoneme, possesses 9 pairs of radially arranged peripheral doublet microtubules and one pair of centrally located microtubules, enclosed by a central sheath, designated as the '$9 + 2$' array.

questions.question: The centrosome contains two cylindrical structures called centrioles that lie perpendicular to each other. The internal organization of a centriole consists of:
options: Cartwheel-like $9 + 0$ arrangement of evenly spaced peripheral triplet tubulin fibrils with a proteinaceous central hub
$9 + 2$ doublet microtubular organization with dynein arms
questions.solution: A centriole has a cartwheel-like organization made of 9 evenly spaced peripheral triplets of tubulin protein with no microtubules in the center ($9 + 0$ arrangement). The proteinaceous central part is called the hub, connected to peripheral triplets via radial spokes.

questions.question: Nuclear pores in the eukaryotic nuclear envelope are formed by the fusion of its two membranes and function as passages for the movement of:
options: RNA and proteins bidirectionally between the nucleus and the cytoplasm
Intact chromosomes into the cytoplasm during interphase
Lipid droplets and lysosomes into the nucleoplasm
DNA molecules to mitochondria for replication
questions.solution: Nuclear pores are minute channels formed by the fusion of the inner and outer nuclear membranes. They facilitate controlled bidirectional transport of RNA and protein molecules between the nucleoplasm and the cytoplasm.

questions.question: The nucleolus is a dense, non-membrane bound colloidal structure present in the nucleoplasm that is the active site for the synthesis of:
questions.solution: The nucleolus is not bounded by a membrane and its content is continuous with the rest of the nucleoplasm. It is the primary active site for ribosomal RNA (rRNA) synthesis.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the morphological classification of chromosomes based on the position of the centromere (primary constriction):

List-I (Chromosome Type)List-II (Centromere Position)
(A) Metacentric(I) Centromere situated close to one end forming one extremely short and one very long arm
(B) Sub-metacentric(II) Terminal centromere situated at the tip of the chromosome
(C) Acrocentric(III) Centromere in the middle forming two equal arms (V-shaped)
(D) Telocentric(IV) Centromere slightly away from the middle forming one slightly shorter and one longer arm (L-shaped)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Metacentric: Middle centromere (two equal arms); Sub-metacentric: Slightly off-center centromere (one shorter and one longer arm); Acrocentric: Sub-terminal centromere close to one end (one very short and one very long arm); Telocentric: Terminal centromere at the tip.

questions.question: Kinetochores are specialized structures on chromosomes characterized as:
options: Disc-shaped proteinaceous structures present on the sides of the primary constriction (centromere)
Non-staining secondary constrictions giving rise to satellite DNA
Terminal protective caps containing repetitive telomeric DNA
Lipid-rich granules holding sister chromatids together
questions.solution: Kinetochores are disc-shaped multi-protein complexes situated on the sides of the primary constriction (centromere) of chromosomes that serve as the attachment sites for spindle fibers during cell division.

questions.question: A non-staining secondary constriction at a constant location on certain chromosomes gives the appearance of a small fragment called a:
questions.solution: A few chromosomes possess non-staining secondary constrictions at constant locations. This gives the appearance of a small distal fragment called a satellite (the chromosome is called a SAT-chromosome).

questions.question: Which of the following cellular organelles are semi-autonomous due to the presence of their own circular DNA, 70S ribosomes, and protein synthesizing machinery?
questions.solution: Mitochondria and Chloroplasts are semi-autonomous organelles possessing their own circular double-stranded DNA, RNA molecules, 70S ribosomes, and enzymatic machinery to synthesize some of their own proteins, reproducing by fission.

questions.question: Microbodies are membrane-bound minute vesicles found in both plant and animal cells that contain:
options: Various oxidative and metabolic enzymes (e.g., Peroxisomes, Glyoxysomes)
RNA and ribosome synthesizing subunits only
questions.solution: Microbodies (e.g., peroxisomes and glyoxysomes) are small, single membrane-bound vesicles distributed in both plant and animal cells that contain enzymes involved in peroxide metabolism, photorespiration, and lipid conversion.

questions.question: Plasmodesmata are microscopic cytoplasmic channels that function to:
options: Connect the cytoplasm of adjacent plant cells across cell walls and middle lamella
Anchor bacterial cells to mucous membranes
Produce secretory proteins in the Golgi cisternae
Store calcium in the smooth endoplasmic reticulum
questions.solution: Plasmodesmata are microscopic cytoplasmic bridges traversing the plant cell wall and middle lamella that connect the cytoplasm of neighboring plant cells for intercellular communication and transport.

questions.question:
Read the following statements regarding the eukaryotic cell membrane:
Statement I: Phospholipids are arranged in a bilayer with their polar hydrophilic heads facing outward and non-polar hydrophobic hydrocarbon tails facing inward.
Statement II: Peripheral proteins lie on the surface of the membrane, while integral proteins are partially or totally buried in the bilayer.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.solution: Both statements are correct according to the Fluid Mosaic Model. Phospholipids form an amphipathic bilayer protecting the hydrophobic fatty acid tails from the aqueous environment, with peripheral proteins resting externally and integral proteins embedded within.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT regarding prokaryotic cells?
options: They possess membrane-bound organelles like mitochondria and Golgi apparatus.
Their genetic material is naked and not enveloped by a nuclear membrane (genophore/nucleoid).
Many bacteria have small circular extra-chromosomal DNA called plasmids.
Ribosomes in prokaryotes are of 70S type associated with the plasma membrane.
questions.solution: Prokaryotic cells lack all membrane-bound organelles (such as ER, Golgi, mitochondria, chloroplasts, and lysosomes). They have 70S ribosomes, a naked nucleoid, and some possess plasmids.

questions.question: The major site for synthesis of glycolipids and glycoproteins in a eukaryotic cell is:
questions.solution: The Golgi apparatus is the primary cellular site for the post-translational modification and synthesis of glycoproteins (glycosylation of proteins) and glycolipids (glycosylation of lipids).

questions.question: Chromatin contains DNA and which of the following proteins?
options: Basic histone proteins and some non-histone proteins along with RNA
Acidic histone proteins and no RNA
questions.solution: Interphase chromatin in eukaryotic nuclei contains genomic DNA, basic (positively charged) histone proteins, some non-histone chromosomal proteins, and small amounts of RNA.

questions.question: A single human cell contains approximately how much length of DNA distributed among its 46 (23 pairs) chromosomes?
questions.solution: A single diploid human cell has approximately 6.6 × 10⁹ base pairs of DNA, which corresponds to a total length of approximately 2.2 metres packaged within a nucleus of ~10 µm diameter.

questions.question: Polysomes (polyribosomes) found in bacterial cells consist of:
options: Several ribosomes attached simultaneously to a single mRNA strand translating it into proteins
Clusters of plasmids attached to mesosomes
Ribosomes attached to the outer nuclear membrane
Aggregations of rRNA and DNA fragments
questions.solution: In prokaryotic translation, several ribosomes can attach to a single strand of mRNA to form a chain-like structure called a polyribosome or polysome, translating the message into multiple copies of the same polypeptide.

questions.question: Which of the following structures is absent in higher plant cells but present in animal cells?
questions.solution: Plant cells possess cell walls, plastids, and a large central vacuole, which are absent in animal cells. Conversely, animal cells possess centrosomes and centrioles (which organize spindle poles during cell division), which are absent in almost all higher plant cells.

questions.question: Gas vacuoles (pseudovacuoles) are found in:
options: Blue-green algae, purple and green photosynthetic bacteria
questions.solution: Gas vacuoles are proteinaceous, non-membrane bound structures found in photosynthetic prokaryotes like blue-green algae and purple/green sulphur photosynthetic bacteria that provide buoyancy in aquatic environments.

questions.question: Both cilia and flagella emerge from centriole-like basal structures called:
questions.solution: Both cilia and flagella are hair-like outgrowths of the cell membrane that arise from centriole-like structures called basal bodies located in the cortex below the plasma membrane.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about cell wall composition is CORRECT?
options: Algae have cell walls made of cellulose, galactans, mannans, and calcium carbonate, while plants have cellulose, hemicellulose, pectins, and proteins.
Fungi have cell walls made of cellulose and peptidoglycan.
Bacterial cell walls are made of cellulose and chitin.
Plant cell walls are made solely of peptidoglycan and teichoic acid.
questions.solution: Algae have cell walls composed of cellulose, galactans, mannans, and minerals like calcium carbonate. Other plants have cell walls composed of cellulose, hemicellulose, pectins, and proteins.

questions.question: The primary cell wall of a young plant cell is characterized by its capability for:
options: Growth and extensibility, which gradually diminishes as the cell matures
Direct fusion into the middle lamella without cellulose microfibrils
questions.solution: The cell wall of a young plant cell, the primary wall, is capable of growth and expansion. It diminishes as the cell matures, and a secondary wall is deposited on the inner (plasma membrane) side of the cell.

questions.question: Which of the following cell sizes is INCORRECTLY matched with its respective biological entity according to NCERT?
options: Human red blood cells (RBCs): ~7.0 µm in diameter
questions.solution: According to NCERT, a typical eukaryotic cell measures 10 to 20 µm in diameter (not 0.1 to 0.5 µm). Mycoplasmas are ~0.3 µm, typical bacteria are 1–2 µm, and human RBCs are ~7.0 µm in diameter.

questions.question: The lumen of the thylakoid in a chloroplast is the site where:
options: Protons ($H^+$ ions) accumulate during light-dependent photosynthetic electron transport
Dark reaction and Calvin cycle synthesis of sugars occurs exclusively
Replication of circular chloroplast DNA takes place
questions.solution: Thylakoids enclose an aqueous space called a lumen. During light-driven photosynthetic electron transport, water photolysis and proton pumping accumulate $H^+$ ions inside the thylakoid lumen, generating a proton gradient for ATP synthesis.

questions.question:
Read the following statements regarding the nucleus and chromatin:
Statement I: Euchromatin is loosely packed, lightly stained, and transcriptionally active chromatin.
Statement II: Heterochromatin is densely packed, darkly stained, and transcriptionally inactive.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.solution: Both statements are correct. In an interphase nucleus, euchromatin refers to the loosely coiled, light-staining, transcriptionally active regions, whereas heterochromatin refers to the tightly condensed, dark-staining, transcriptionally silent chromosomal regions.

questions.question: The space between the two parallel membranes of the eukaryotic nuclear envelope is called the perinuclear space, which measures approximately:
questions.solution: The nuclear envelope consists of two parallel lipid bilayer membranes separated by a 10 to 50 nm wide fluid-filled space called the perinuclear space, which forms a barrier between the nucleoplasm and cytoplasm.

questions.question: Plasmids present in many bacterial cells are defined as:
options: Small, circular, self-replicating, double-stranded extra-chromosomal DNA molecules conferring specific phenotypic traits like antibiotic resistance
Linear single-stranded RNA fragments attached to ribosomes
Infoldings of the bacterial cell membrane used for respiration
Proteinaceous storage granules containing phosphate reserves
questions.solution: In addition to the main genomic DNA, many bacteria have small, circular, self-replicating, double-stranded extra-chromosomal DNA molecules called plasmids. Plasmids carry non-essential genes that confer unique phenotypic advantages, such as resistance to specific antibiotics.
